title: Meet the Young Homeowners Beating the Odds in a Crazy Expensive Market!
summary:
Did you know the average age of first-time homebuyers in the U.S. is now 40? That sounds pretty old, right? But a small group of young people in their 20s—called Gen Z—are managing to buy homes anyway. And they're doing it in some pretty clever ways!

Meet Francisco Vazquez. He's 27 and just bought a cute yellow three-bedroom house in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. It has a basement, a garage, and a yard. He paid $220,000, which is almost half the national median price. But here's the amazing part: he saved up $72,000 in just over two years! How? He changed careers, lived with his parents rent-free for a year, and stuck to a super strict budget. He even sanded and stained the hardwood floors himself to save money.

Vazquez isn't alone. More Gen Zers are becoming homeowners, even though houses are really expensive right now. In fact, 4% of homebuyers last year were Gen Z, up from 3% the year before. And they're different from millennials: they're more likely to buy on their own (especially women), less likely to get help from their parents, and they use social media to learn about money.

Vazquez had to make some tough choices. He loved his old jobs rescuing alligators and working at a zoo, but the pay was too low. So he switched to managing a fast food restaurant, which paid better and had good benefits. His wife helped him balance saving with having fun. Now, with a 15-year mortgage, his big goal is to retire early. "Buying a home helps me buy myself more freedom," he says. Pretty inspiring, right?
why_it_matters: Even when things seem too expensive, setting goals and making smart money choices can help you achieve big dreams like owning a home.

background_read: The national median home price in the U.S. is over $400,000, making it very hard for young people to afford a house without careful planning.
Gen Z is the generation born roughly from 1997 to 2012; they are now in their 20s and entering the housing market.
Milwaukee, Wisconsin, is a city in the Midwest where home prices are often lower than on the East or West Coasts, which helped Vazquez buy a home.
A mortgage is a special loan for buying a house; a 15-year mortgage like Vazquez has means he will pay it off in half the usual time, but with higher monthly payments.
Article_Structure: WHO: Francisco Vazquez and other Gen Z homebuyers in their 20s
WHAT: Young people using clever strategies like career changes, strict budgets, and do-it-yourself repairs to buy homes despite high prices
WHERE: Milwaukee, Wisconsin, but the trend is seen across the United States
WHY: They want financial freedom and a stable place to live, and are willing to make big sacrifices to reach that goal

perspectives.description: They prove that by living on a tight budget, switching to better-paying jobs, and learning from social media, it’s possible to buy a house earlier than the average age.
The fact that the average homebuyer is now 40 shows how much harder it is for younger generations to afford a place, raising concerns about inequality.
They note that areas with lower median prices, like parts of the Midwest, offer a more realistic path to homeownership for Generation Z compared to expensive coastal cities.
